classification.difficultyReason: Calculate an interior angle from an exterior angle and compare the complete angle sets to reject similarity.

content.prompt: Give reasons why the two triangles in these diagrams are not similar.

spec.description: Two horizontally paired triangles with the source baseline extensions. A leader identifies the interior angle at D. Ordinary source-blue geometry is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: A, B and C are collinear in that order. Angle DAB is 50 degrees and angle ADB is 110 degrees. Z, Y and X are collinear in that order; W lies below their line. Exterior angle ZYW is 165 degrees and interior angle YWX is 110 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; calculated angles are confined to answers.

answer.short: Not similar: the angle sets are $50^\circ,110^\circ,20^\circ$ and $15^\circ,110^\circ,55^\circ$. Corresponding angles are not all equal.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle DBA&=180^\circ-50^\circ-110^\circ\\&=20^\circ\\\angle XYW&=180^\circ-165^\circ\\&=15^\circ\\\angle YXW&=180^\circ-110^\circ-15^\circ\\&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angle sets are $50^\circ,110^\circ,20^\circ$ and $15^\circ,110^\circ,55^\circ$. Corresponding angles are not all equal, so the triangles are not similar.
